# scm_dlp_dictionary (Resource)

Manages an Enterprise DLP Keyword Dictionary.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A custom keyword dictionary. Keywords are uploaded as a file on create and
# update. If keyword_list is omitted on update, the existing keywords are kept.
resource "scm_dlp_dictionary" "project_codenames" {
  name               = "Internal-Project-Codenames"
  description        = "Confidential project codenames"
  category           = "Confidential"
  region_name        = "us"
  original_file_name = "codenames.txt"
  is_case_sensitive  = false
  keyword_list       = ["ProjectApollo", "ProjectOrion", "ProjectCentaurus"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `category` (String) Category of the dictionary (e.g., Confidential, Financial, Healthcare, etc.).
- `name` (String) The name of the dictionary.
- `original_file_name` (String) Original file name of the dictionary file (.txt or .csv).
- `region_name` (String) Region for the dictionary (e.g. us, eu).

### Optional

- `description` (String) A description of the dictionary.
- `is_case_sensitive` (Boolean) Whether keyword matching is case sensitive.
- `keyword_list` (List of String) List of keywords belonging to this dictionary. When omitted, the existing keywords are kept on update. Keywords must not have leading or trailing whitespace.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of the dictionary.
- `keyword_count` (Number) Total number of keywords in the dictionary.
- `tfid` (String) The Terraform ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing DLP dictionary by its ID.
terraform import scm_dlp_dictionary.example <id>
```
